subject: Hosted quickstart vs Dedicated/Private — deployment path & rateband follow-up
messages:

Subject: Quick follow-up after demo — deployment questions

Evelyn,

Thanks again for the demo this morning — the model throughput looked promising. A few follow-ups from our side after we regrouped:

- Primary question: for our pilot (1M tokens/month, ~500 concurrent users at peak) do you still recommend Hosted API, or should we plan for Dedicated capacity from day one? Our security team also asked about VPC/private options — is that a blocker for pilot?
- Can you confirm what "endpoints" we should use for the pilot? We're planning two main flows: short-form generations (customer chat) and embeddings for search/recall.
- What's the default rateband for the hosted quickstart (requests/sec and token windows)? We want to know if we need to throttle on our side or rely on Redwood's burst handling.

I've attached our initial security checklist and the compliance contact is Alice (alice.chen@clearpod.ai) — she'll loop in legal if needed.

Next step: can you send a concise mutual action plan and the endpoints/rate numbers so our infra lead can sign off? Happy to schedule a 30-min follow-up next week.

From: Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.ai>

Cc: aditya.rao@redwood.ai, monica.patel@redwood.ai
Date: Fri, 6 Nov 2026 10:04:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Quick follow-up after demo — deployment questions

Samir — great to hear and thanks for the checklist. Quick recap and recommended path based on what you described: 

1) Pilot recommendation: Hosted API quickstart
   - For 1M tokens/month and the concurrency profile you described, Hosted is the fastest path to value. It gives you immediate endpoints, automatic scaling for short bursts, and removes the ops burden while you validate quality and UX.
   - Dedicated is appropriate once you need sustained predictable throughput with an SLA and isolated capacity (typically later-stage pilots or production with >10M tokens/month or strict isolation requirements).
   - Private (VPC/on-prem) is available but involves longer lead time (networking, entitlements, and potentially on-prem packaging). Not necessary for an exploratory pilot unless legal requires it.

2) Endpoints to map for pilot (recommended):
   - /v1/generate (for streaming and chat-style responses)
   - /v1/embeddings (for semantic search and rerank)
   - /v1/rerank (optional; we can proxy reranker as a single call if you prefer)

3) Default hosted quickstart rateband (recommended starting config):
   - Generations (/v1/generate): 150 reqs/s sustained per account, burst to 300 reqs/s for short windows (handled by the runtime). Token-based soft limits: ~600k tokens/minute across the account before we trigger token throttles.
   - Embeddings (/v1/embeddings): 250 reqs/s sustained, burst to 600 reqs/s (embeddings are cheaper per-token and more parallel-friendly).
   - We recommend client-side exponential backoff + 429 retry logic. Redwood's hosted runtime has automatic short-term burst smoothing; for sustained traffic you should plan on batching (embeddings) and prefix-KV caching for repeated prompts.

Attachments: I attached a short hosted quickstart playbook with the exact steps for sandbox access, endpoint names, sample curl snippets, and a mutual action plan template.

Next steps I propose:
- You confirm who will receive sandbox creds (email list) so we can provision endpoints.
- Alice (compliance) — if you can share specific checklist items that would be blockers for pilot, we can flag them and share the Private/VPC readiness timeline.
- Schedule a 30-min call early next week to provision the sandbox and run a traffic-pattern smoke test.

If you want, I can loop in our solutions engineer (Aditya) to clarify the VPC/private effort estimates.

Best,
Evelyn Hart
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

Attachment: Redwood_Hosted_Quickstart_Playbook.pdf (application/pdf)

Samir — quick answers below so your infra and UX teams can move forward: 

- Hosted latency SLOs: for short prompts (<=128 tokens) our hosted runtime targets 95th percentile token latency under 200ms when under the recommended ratebands. For streaming we provide chunked streaming with ~1-2 token batches; end-to-end latency will also depend on model choice and prompt size. If you need a stricter SLO we can discuss Dedicated profiles that guarantee lower tail latencies.

- Embeddings batching guidance: we recommend batching where possible. Typical tradeoffs:
  * Small single-row calls: ~50–120ms median when routed to an embeddings-optimized pool (depends on model).
  * Batch sizes of 16–64 are common for throughput with ~100–200ms tail depending on model and GPU.
  * We provide SDK helpers in the quickstart that implement adaptive batching and concurrency for embeddings — we'll include example config in the playbook.

Operational notes:
- Prefix/KV caching is mostly applicable to generation endpoints; embeddings benefit more from batching and caching vector lookups on your side.
- If compliance requires VPC, the typical timeline for Private deployment is 6–8 weeks (networking, entitlements, and validation). We can run the pilot in Hosted while parallelizing Private readiness checks to avoid blocking.

I'll open a short mutual action plan in HubSpot (link below) and provision sandbox creds once you confirm recipients. Aditya — can you add an estimate for VPC private timeline in the hubspot note?

Looping in a short VPC/Private feasibility note: 

- If ClearPod's compliance items require dedicated network egress controls (IP allowlisting + private peering), Private (VPC) is the right path. Estimated lift: 6 weeks (if no unusual legal constraints), or 8–10 weeks if your security team requires an HSM/KMS integration and SOC evidence collection.
- For your pilot, my recommendation is to run Hosted quickstart immediately (no VPC) and run a parallel Private readiness track — that minimizes time-to-value while keeping compliance on the critical path.
- I'll add a short checklist to the HubSpot deal with the networking artifacts we'll need (ASN, peering contact, expected CIDR blocks).

Happy to jump on a call with Alice and Samir next week to walk through the checklist.

—Aditya
